summary: Build practical mine closure, rehabilitation and environmental management skills in 5 days. Create plans, scorecards, and reporting packs.
lede: Mine closure and rehabilitation involves planning how disturbed mine areas will be stabilized, restored and monitored for agreed post-mining uses. For mine environmental, rehabilitation and closure professionals, this course covers assessing closure readiness, sequencing progressive rehabilitation, and establishing monitoring and reporting. Practical work includes closure risk assessments, rehabilitation plans, monitoring templates, cost provisioning, and stakeholder engagement.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already work around mine environmental performance, rehabilitation delivery, or closure governance and need a more structured way to plan and report closure work.
prerequisites: You should bring a laptop, a calculator or spreadsheet tool, and a working understanding of mine environmental issues such as erosion, dust, water management, biodiversity, and decommissioning. If available, bring recent site closure notes, monitoring summaries, or rehabilitation photos so you can apply the templates directly to your own operational context.
